summary: A 1969 note by Vint Cerf on the control links used between IMPs and between hosts. Its text indicates concern about interference with communication between IMPs. It is an early working note, not a standard.

eli5.summary: This note is about the special lanes used for control messages between the network boxes and between computers, so regular traffic does not get in their way.

questions: imp imp and host host control links
host host and imp imp communication
subtitle: A proposal to segregate control traffic between network processors from regular Host communication.

tldr.problem: On early ARPANET, control messages between IMPs and between Hosts competed for the same links as regular user data, causing delays in critical control traffic.
tldr.mechanism: Vint Cerf proposes using link 0 exclusively for IMP-to-IMP control and link 1 for Host-to-Host control, ensuring control messages are never delayed by regular traffic.
tldr.outcome: The idea of segregated control channels was adopted in ARPANET design. This principle persists in modern networks where control and data planes are managed separately.

today: This RFC is a historical note from 1969. The specific link assignments it proposes are no longer relevant, but the principle it embodies—that control and data traffic should be segregated—remains central to modern network design. Today's networks implement this through virtualization, separate physical interfaces, or protocol mechanisms.

sections.title: Segregating Control Traffic
sections.content: Vint Cerf proposes that the ARPANET reserve specific links for control communications. Link 0 would carry only IMP-to-IMP control messages, and link 1 would carry Host-to-Host control messages. Regular user data would use other links. This separation prevents control messages from being delayed when the network becomes congested with user traffic.
sections.eli5: Like having a special highway for emergency vehicles so they do not get stuck in traffic jams.

sections.title: Link Assignment
sections.content: The proposal specifies two dedicated links: link 0 for IMP-to-IMP control, carrying messages about network state and routing decisions between the network processors themselves, and link 1 for Host-to-Host control, enabling direct communication between user systems without router involvement. This two-level separation addresses both inter-router coordination and user-level communication.
sections.eli5: Think of it as a three-lane road: one lane just for trucks talking to trucks, one just for cars talking to cars, and all other lanes for regular traffic.

sections.title: Lasting Principle
sections.content: This early insight into network design—that control traffic and data traffic should be managed separately—became a fundamental principle of networking. Modern networks maintain separate control planes (where routing and management decisions happen) from data planes (where user traffic flows). This separation ensures that the network can manage itself even when congested or under attack.
sections.eli5: The idea that control messages need special treatment became the foundation for how networks manage themselves when things get busy.
